reason: First question list for the migration of the question system into the running instance. The node frontier records only what holds where; these questions ask what the object is like at the places where every method has become tight, and why. Each is grounded in published records read in the original, and conjectural parts are marked as such.

questions.statement: In the window t = (n-2k)/k^(2/3) around the center, independently measured landmarks fall close together: the peak of d = b_{n,k}-b_{n,k-1} at t* ~ 2.05 (the mode of f_S), the sign change of the chain excess X'' at ~2.09, the failure of the published bound K''(k) > J^G at t ~ 2.1-2.5 while d itself stays large and positive, the peak of the relative-second-difference profile at t ~ 2.59, and the maximum ~2.25 of the moment ratio R at t ~ 4; towards t -> 0 the capacity-response of the mean rises to 50-80% of E[Z]^2 and the margin of every method shrinks, while for t in a fixed interval [t_0, T] the moment margin stays O(1). What is the limiting structure of this window - the laws of d, mu, R and the response ratio rho as functions of t - and why does the reach of the one-heavy-block environment J^G coincide with the mode of f_S? A sufficient answer derives the window profiles from a two-component (or other) limit law, explains the coincidence of the landmarks or shows it to be accidental, and identifies the quantity that makes t -> 0 the tightest point for the central proof, the right-side proof, and the left-side moment tests alike.
questions.grounds: r1b79fab... section 6: f_S has mode t* = 2.0515 and the window profile of mu is f_S(t)/E(S-t)_+ with maximum at t ~ 2.59; conjecture LW states the pointwise window law; the review feedback (section 7) flags that the producer's d-peak at 2.09k^(2/3) sits at the same place as two quantities in r475ada... section 7 and that the common cause is an open question. r475ada... section 7: X'' becomes negative at nu ~ 2.09k^(2/3) and K''(k)-J^G at nu ~ 2.1-2.5k^(2/3), while d is positive and large there; the true-marker comparison K''(k) > J_n(k-1) holds everywhere measured with d to relative 10^(-4), so the loss lives entirely in replacing J by J^G (binary64 map, exact for small k). r6b37c7e... sections 5.4 and 6.6: the moment ratio R has a k-independent window profile with maximum ~2.25-2.27 at t ~ 4, tends to 1 as t -> 0 like (2/I_0)k^(-1/3), and the limit function of this profile was not derived. r10ff8c2... sections 5.5 and 5.7: the tightest point of the left moment window is its left end n = 2k+41; the exact identity T = E_k^2 + Delta_1 + Delta_2 shows the second-stage cancellation survives only in a boundary layer t < 0.5-1 where the capacity response of the mean reaches 0.5-0.8 of E^2, with the conjecture e' = e^2/2 for the limit profile. rce3dc75... section 10, r8a9b11e... section 3.3, ra4c01fc... section 10.3: the center is the tightest point of the central proof, of the right-side proof (limit ratio 1.795 at lambda = 1/2) and of the unfolded central method (eta = 1 hardest). All landmark values are binary64 observations; the coincidence is unexplained.

questions.statement: The right half (n < 2k) is now informally proved and the left half (n > 2k) is what remains of the root. At the center the two sides differ structurally: the first-layer profile Phi_2 vanishes linearly at lambda = 1/2 so the moment-margin constant stays finite (2/I_0), whereas the second-layer profile Phi_3 diverges like delta^(-1/2) and the constant grows like 1.198/delta; on the right the vertices of size > k form a single chain with H_k <= 1 and the proof could sum over the start row and reverse time to turn conditioned bridges into an unconditioned killed Borel walk, whereas on the left they form a tree with side branches, H_k can exceed 1, and the one-heavy-block environment fails at nu ~ 2.5k^(2/3). Which structural property of left-half configurations - the second component above capacity, the side branches, or something else - is responsible for the extra difficulty, and does the right-side device (unconditioning by time reversal, absorption of the top row) have a left-half analogue? A sufficient answer identifies the responsible structure and either gives a left-half representation with the same unconditioning effect or an argument why none exists.
questions.grounds: r6b37c7e... section 6.5: proved endpoint constants show m_3 diverges at both ends of the second layer while the first-layer constant m(1/2+) = 2/I_0 is finite, with the asymmetry traced to Phi_2 vanishing linearly and Phi_3 growing like delta^(-1/2) at the center. r8a9b11e... sections 3.2-3.3, 4.2-4.4, 7: the right-side proof succeeds by absorbing the top row, setting alpha = 0, and the time-reversal identity RW; the center is its tightest point (limit ratio 1.795) and the record lists row-wise bridge variance as the obstacle that reversal bypassed. r20df549... section 7: on the left the heavy vertices form a tree, so the endpoint decomposition must become a leaf-wise decomposition; not attempted. r9d97cea... section 8.2: side branches appear for n > 2k and the restricted response's asymptotics are open. r5f5cf73... section 4: the central Gaussian method unfolds over the entire right half because t = 1 is a critical point for every n; no left analogue is stated. r475ada... section 7: the published left bound fails at nu ~ 2.1-2.5k^(2/3) only because the restricted environment is replaced by a one-heavy-block environment. This question differs from op-tie-block-transport (which asks for the pairing) and op-layer-period (which asks for the layer constants): it asks what structural feature separates the two halves. Interpretive; conjectural.
